title: Policy approval core
description: Objective: implement four-outcome policy evaluation, R0-R3 risk tiers, exact-hash approval decisions, and selective invalidation. Deliverable: packages/core policy modules with decision-table and property tests. NOT in scope: mutable UI policy editing, budgets, provider execution, or global speed modes. Hard dependencies: Runtime contract registry and Planning graph lifecycle core. Owned paths: packages/core/src/policy/**. Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/core typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/core test.
definitionOfDone: Policy produces ALLOW, REQUIRE_APPROVAL, DENY, or HOLD_UNKNOWN with stable reason codes.
Unknown or missing inputs can never become ALLOW and caller risk labels cannot lower daemon-derived risk.
Approvals bind exact hashes/scope/policy/actor and invalidate only the proven impact set.
The focused core typecheck and test command exits 0.
taskRails: Follow the pinned design; this task cannot create authority beyond its named contract.
Fail closed with stable codes and immutable deterministic outputs.
Keep production modules focused, target <=250 lines, split before 400.
Use TDD and stage only explicit owned paths; no worktree, broad add, push, or merge.

12 decision-table cases written against the not-yet-existing surface (evaluatePolicy + policy-contract types):
1. Every outcome reachable with a stable local reason code — ALLOW/ALLOWED_BY_POLICY, DENY/DENIED_BY_RULE, REQUIRE_HUMAN_APPROVAL/HUMAN_ONLY_TIER, HOLD_UNKNOWN/REQUIRED_FACT_MISSING.
2. UNKNOWN-never-ALLOW over 8 permutations: absent required fact; truthClass UNKNOWN; OBSERVED; AGENT_REPORTED; tier-less fact; hint+absent; waiver+absent; waiver+UNKNOWN. The last two are the waiver-laundering paths (design 712) folded into the same permutation table rather than a separate case.
3/4/5. riskHint settlement: hint R3 raises effectiveTier while computedTier stays R0; hint R0 CANNOT lower a computed R2; hint appears in neither inputFacts nor usedFactIds; and the mandatory case hint=R2 + missing fact -> still HOLD_UNKNOWN with computedTier/effectiveTier both null.
6. Lattice DENY > HOLD_UNKNOWN > REQUIRE_HUMAN_APPROVAL > ALLOW asserted pairwise.
7. Slice-chain relaxation refused across four shapes: effect weakened DENY->ALLOW; parent obligation dropped; obligation kind downgraded HARD->SOFT; child ADDING an auto-approval opt-in the parent lacks (adding an opt-in is a relaxation, so the effective opt-in set can only shrink down the chain).
8. Waiver accepted ONLY when {namedObligationId resolves to a parent SOFT obligation, scope subset-of decision scope, expiry strictly after evaluatedAtEpochMs, humanApprovalRef non-empty}; four invalid shapes each -> DENY, and out-of-scope additionally carries WAIVER_INVALID.
9. Auto path structurally unavailable above R1: a forged R2 opt-in is an INPUT_INVALID REJECTION (not a decision), and R2/R3 facts yield REQUIRE_HUMAN_APPROVAL even with an R1 opt-in present.
10. R3 carries HARD obligations core.decision_reason_required + core.step_up_authentication_required; a slice with no opt-in defaults to REQUIRE_HUMAN_APPROVAL/AUTO_APPROVAL_NOT_OPTED_IN (no blanket-ALLOW path).
11. Provenance recorded (policyRevisionRef, evaluatorVersion, action, graphNodeRevisionRefs, decisionDigest, matchedRuleIds), record + nested arrays deep-frozen, repeat evaluation deep-equal.
12. Malformed input -> INPUT_INVALID (null input, non-hex64 digest, NaN clock, duplicate factId, empty slice chain). INPUT_INVALID is sourceless in the registry, so this is the code that actually surfaces rather than degrading.

Two design settlements the test now pins, both fail-closed and documented in step-3's module header:
- A tier-contributing fact must clear the strongTruth floor (DAEMON_VERIFIED|HUMAN_APPROVED). OBSERVED/AGENT_REPORTED are not daemon-derived, so they are "unclassifiable" per design 11.6 and yield HOLD_UNKNOWN rather than grounding a tier.
- No tier-contributing fact at all -> computedTier null -> HOLD_UNKNOWN. Absence of classification is never silently R0.

EVALUATION SHAPE. evaluatePolicy(unknown) folds FOUR independent layers onto the lattice:
1. evidence — required fact absent / truthClass UNKNOWN / tier-bearing fact below the strong-truth floor -> HOLD_UNKNOWN;
2. relaxation — a child slice weakening a parent rule or obligation, or declaring an auto-approval opt-in no ancestor covers -> DENY;
3. rules — the effective rule set's strongest effect (DENIED_BY_RULE / REQUIRE_HUMAN_APPROVAL_BY_RULE);
4. tier — R2/R3 human-only, R0/R1 need an explicit opt-in match on (action, tier).
The safety property is STRUCTURAL, not a special case: HOLD_UNKNOWN sits above both REQUIRE_HUMAN_APPROVAL and ALLOW in the lattice, so no lower layer can lift an unknown into an allowance, and a waiver only ever suppresses a layer-2 relaxation, so a waiver has no reachable path to convert HOLD_UNKNOWN into ALLOW (design 712).

FOUR MODELLING SETTLEMENTS, each fail-closed:
- effectiveTier = computedTier === null ? null : max(computedTier, hint). A hint therefore cannot manufacture a tier out of an unclassifiable assessment; it can only raise one that facts already established. computedTier, callerRiskHint, and effectiveTier are all recorded separately for audit.
- Rule inheritance is DECLARATION-BASED: a child that stays silent about a parent rule inherits it (silence is not removal), but a child that REDECLARES it must do so at equal or greater strength. Redeclaring at a weaker effect, dropping any HARD obligation, or downgrading HARD -> SOFT is a relaxation; only a dropped SOFT obligation is waivable.
- The effective auto-approval opt-in set is the LAST slice's declaration, so omitting an inherited opt-in is a tightening and re-declaring one an ancestor never granted is a relaxation. Combined with the R0/R1-only type on PolicyAutoApprovalOptIn, there is no reachable blanket-ALLOW: ALLOW requires a classified R0/R1 tier AND an explicit action-matched opt-in AND no unknown evidence AND no relaxation AND no DENY/RHA rule.
- Waiver coverage requires namedObligationId equality, expiresAtEpochMs STRICTLY greater than evaluatedAtEpochMs (expiry exactly at evaluation time is expired — tested), and scope subset-of decision scope. A waiver offered for the dropped obligation but failing any of these adds WAIVER_INVALID alongside SLICE_RELAXATION_DETECTED so the audit distinguishes "no waiver" from "bad waiver".

REGISTRY DISCIPLINE. The only createRuntimeError call in this module is `{ code: "INPUT_INVALID" }` with NO source. INPUT_INVALID declares an empty validSources, and runtime-error-factory.ts:83 requires the source key to be ABSENT for such codes — attaching {aggregate:'APPROVAL'} would have degraded silently to UNKNOWN_ERROR. The test asserts the literal string "INPUT_INVALID" on five malformed shapes, so that degrade cannot land unnoticed.

TWO TEST FIXTURE CORRECTIONS made during implementation, both real defects in the step-2 RED file, not the implementation bending to the test:
- Four cases overrode `facts` with a differently-named fact while leaving requiredFactIds ["fact.read_only"], which would have made every one of them trivially HOLD_UNKNOWN and hidden the tier assertions they were written to make. All four now vary the tier on the SAME required fact id.
- The waiver case `humanApprovalRef: ""` expected DENY, but an empty ref fails the structural guard, so it is an INPUT_INVALID refusal (strictly more fail-closed). It is now asserted as such, and the freed slot covers a sharper semantic case: expiry strictly before evaluation time, next to the boundary case of expiry exactly at it.

Carry-forward invalidation conditions per design 265, all six: any mismatch, missing dependency, changed applicable policy slice, changed predecessor result, changed environment/runtime closure, unknown canonicalization -> carry-forward INVALID. LIFECYCLE (design 360). PENDING -> DECIDED | WITHDRAWN, and both targets are terminal for the lifecycle: DECIDED has no outgoing edge (so `decision` is immutable once set) and WITHDRAWN has none either. Every lifecycle refusal is ILLEGAL_TRANSITION with source {aggregate:"APPROVAL", state: <lifecycle>} and details {aggregateKind, commandKind, sourceState}. The test asserts the LITERAL code plus truthClass DAEMON_VERIFIED plus all three sanitized detail keys — that is the assertion that would catch a silent UNKNOWN_ERROR degrade, since UNKNOWN_ERROR carries truthClass UNKNOWN and empty details. Verified against the registry: ILLEGAL_TRANSITION's validSources include APPROVAL; EXPECTED_VERSION_CONFLICT and IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT do NOT, so neither is used anywhere in this module.

WHY FOUR RECORD INVARIANTS LIVE IN THE GUARD, NOT THE TRANSITION. A record violating any of them was never a legal approval, so it must be unrepresentable rather than merely un-transitionable: (1) decision non-null IFF lifecycle DECIDED; (2) a HUMAN record is HUMAN_APPROVED and always names a stepUpAuthRef — design 718 scopes step-up to every human approval, not just R3; (3) a SYSTEM_POLICY record is DAEMON_VERIFIED never HUMAN_APPROVED (701), confined to R0/R1 (710), names its policyDecisionRef, and carries NO stepUpAuthRef — a daemon principal cannot have authenticated at a terminal; (4) a SYSTEM_POLICY actor matches /^policy:[0-9a-f]{64}$/ literally (701). Six forged SYSTEM_POLICY records are each asserted INPUT_INVALID. R3 additionally requires a non-null decisionReason at decide time (that one IS a transition rule, since the reason arrives with the command).

SELECTIVE INVALIDATION (DoD 3). applyApprovalInvalidation validates and applies a SUPPLIED impact set; it never computes one, because design 265 makes the graph diff the daemon's job and the diff needs the whole graph. Precedence is deliberate and tested: validity !== CURRENT -> untouched (an already settled approval is never relabelled, design 269) > explicit successor linkage -> SUPERSEDED > impact-set intersection on exactRevisionHash or approvedNodeScope -> INVALIDATED > otherwise CURRENT. The SUPERSEDED and INVALIDATED paths take DIFFERENT evidence, and the test pins that by feeding an approval that both intersects the impact set AND has a successor link: it comes back SUPERSEDED, not INVALIDATED. An impact set whose canonicalizerVersion is not in supportedCanonicalizerVersions is refused outright with INPUT_INVALID and NO approval is touched (design 250/265 fail-closed).

ONE DELIBERATE TEST CHANGE, argued rather than accommodated. The RED file asserted reference identity (`toBe`) for a non-intersecting approval. Reference identity is unachievable without handing back the caller's own mutable object straight through the hostile-input boundary, which would be a real regression in exchange for a stronger-looking assertion. The property that actually matters is that the approval is unperturbed, so it is now asserted as `toEqual(untouched)` AND `not.toBe(untouched)` AND `Object.isFrozen`. That is strictly stronger: it proves value preservation, proves the input array was not mutated in place, and proves the output is frozen. Every returned record is a fresh frozen copy.

CARRY-FORWARD. evaluateCarryForward reports ALL failing conditions rather than short-circuiting on the first, so an operator sees the whole reason a reuse was refused. All six design-265 conditions are covered one-to-one by CARRY_FORWARD_* codes and each is asserted individually: hash mismatch, missing dependency, changed policy slice, changed predecessor result, changed environment/runtime closure, unknown canonicalization. A clean input returns exactly {reasonCodes: [], valid: true}; a malformed one (non-hex64 sourceHash) is an INPUT_INVALID rejection rather than a defaulted verdict.

ADVERSARIAL RED-TEAM — the six planned attacks, plus the skill's checklist. Three REAL defects found and fixed, each with a regression test; they are the reason this step was worth running.

FIX 1 (input hardening, policy-validation.ts). My `exact()` used `Object.hasOwn` where the landed planning version checks the property DESCRIPTOR for enumerable + "value" in it, inside a try/catch. Since validObligation/validFact/validRule/validOptIn/validSlice/validWaiver are all EXPORTED, a future caller can reach them with a value that never passed through snapshotData, where an accessor or non-enumerable own key would have satisfied hasOwn and slipped through. Restored to the landed shape.

FIX 2 (unguarded second parameter, approval-invalidation.ts). `evaluateCarryForward(value, supportedCanonicalizerVersions)` snapshotted its first argument but took the second as a trusted `readonly string[]` and called `.includes` on it directly. `evaluateCarryForward` is exported from the ROOT INDEX, so the second argument is caller-controlled: an array with a hostile getter would have thrown out of the function instead of returning a rejection, turning a fail-closed refusal into an exception. Now snapshotted and validated (array, non-empty, every entry a non-empty ref), with four rejection cases tested: malformed input, empty list, null, empty-string entry.

FIX 3 (missing authority gate, approval-invalidation.ts). applyApprovalCommand only checked `lifecycle === "PENDING"`. A record that is PENDING but already INVALIDATED or SUPERSEDED would therefore have DECIDED cleanly, producing a decided-but-invalidated approval — exactly the "settled approval regains authority" shape design 269 forbids. Now refuses ILLEGAL_TRANSITION when validity !== CURRENT, before the lifecycle check, for both decide and withdraw. Tested for both settled validities.

EXPECTED_VERSION_CONFLICT and IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT appear nowhere. The refusal test asserts code + truthClass DAEMON_VERIFIED + all three detail keys, so a degrade to UNKNOWN_ERROR (truthClass UNKNOWN, empty details) fails loudly.
(d) Decision immutability and validity direction — DECIDED and WITHDRAWN both terminal; invalidation never returns a validity to CURRENT and skips settled records entirely.
